sentence: This project builds a system that measures forces made by tissues in real time and uses them to control forces on the tissue.
This project studies how the nasal sensory experience of intranasal cocaine affects the brain and behavior.
This project develops ways to measure cancer metabolism using mass spectrometry and isotope tracing to reveal tumor metabolic activity.
This project uses mouse models and human postmortem tissue to study how epigenetic changes in aging may steer normal aging toward Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how three genes form a feedback loop that drives the growth and spread of a nerve sheath tumor.
This project works to make polygenic scores more accurate and useful across different populations.
This project uses a non-infectious, self-replicative system to screen for antiviral compounds and to study drug resistance.
This project studies how a DNA damage response protein controls the repair of double strand breaks in human cells.
This project studies how the HIV capsid interacts with host proteins as it moves along microtubules and enters the nucleus.
This project studies how an RNA molecule maintains X chromosome inactivation in immune cells.
This project builds models that read electronic health records to spot patients with a genetic form of chronic kidney disease early.
This project develops a drug treatment using biodegradable polymer nanoparticles and laser irradiation to prevent breast cancer tumors from growing back.
This project develops a magnetic resonance fingerprinting exam to describe cardiomyopathy and tests it in patients.
This project studies how benzene exposure affects atherosclerosis and which molecular mechanisms are involved.
This project covers the physics and engineering of magnetic resonance imaging, including image acquisition, processing and clinical translation.
This project builds a high-performance system that speeds up deep neural networks, connectome building and image reconstruction in medical imaging.
This project studies how Hodgkin Lymphoma leads to glomerular injury and albuminuria in nephrotic syndrome.
This project studies how enteric inflammation and cross-reactive T cells lead to acute anterior uveitis, linking the gut and the eye.
This project uses DNA sequencing of human genome regions that shape immune response to study why transplanted kidneys are rejected.
This project studies the molecular identity of channels found in exosomes and their possible role in cardioprotection.
